ai.description: The Assam Indonesian Treefrog reaches 4–5 cm. It is brown with a mottled, moss-like pattern and features prominent, fleshy skin fringes on its limbs and distinct, enlarged toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Theloderma moloch* is uniquely distinguished by the prominent, elongated, horn-like tubercles above its eyes, which are more pronounced than in any other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Theloderma moloch* inhabits primary evergreen tropical forests in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 500 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Theloderma moloch is primarily nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for small insects among the mossy branches of its humid, high-altitude forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Theloderma moloch* is an oviparous species that breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in water-filled tree holes.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Theloderma moloch* is restricted to the evergreen forests of Northeast India, specifically in the states of Assam and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations of 200–1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Assam Indonesian Treefrog emits a series of soft, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard echoing from within dense, humid forest vegetation near breeding pools.
